title: Appeal of RE Scott Robar v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Adopted: the SJC found Case 2004-9 judicially out of order because it was not properly filed under BCO 42-4; the appeal was therefore dismissed without merits review. Vote: 17 concurring, 4 dissenting, 2 recused, 1 absent. The four dissenters would excuse the filing defect because the presbytery clerk gave incorrect advice, Robar relied on it, and Presbytery requested that the appeal be considered timely, citing Plowman as comparable.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed RE Robar's appeal from Central Carolina Presbytery because he filed his notice of appeal with the presbytery's clerk but not with the General Assembly's stated clerk under BCO 42-4. The dissent argued that the presbytery clerk's bad advice and Presbytery's request to treat the appeal as timely should excuse the defect.
summary: The SJC found RE Scott Robar's appeal from Central Carolina Presbytery judicially out of order and dismissed it because he filed his notice of appeal only with Presbytery's stated clerk, not also with the General Assembly's stated clerk as BCO 42-4 requires. No merits review of his conviction occurred. Four commissioners dissented, arguing that the presbytery clerk's admittedly incorrect advice, Robar's reliance, and Presbytery's request to treat the appeal as timely should excuse the filing defect under the Plowman precedent and equity or estoppel principles.
